subject: Dedicated capacity recap - PulseMed (post-call)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap - PulseMed (post-call)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of pain & goals
- Latency spikes during peak clinical hours (affecting triage workflows). Target: p95 < 300ms for ~512-token requests.
- Data isolation & PHI: must run in a private VPC with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and no shared tenant access.
- Predictable throughput for scheduled batch jobs + burst for peak windows.
- Ops: desire SLA-backed uptime and audit logs for compliance.

Recommended dedicated capacity configuration
- Reserved pool: 4 A100 GPUs baseline (supports steady-state concurrency for current volume).
- Burst capacity: ability to scale to 12 GPUs for scheduled peaks / batch windows.
- Isolation: Private deployment (VPC peering) with optional on-prem connector if needed for air-gapped jobs.
- SLAs: 99.9% monthly uptime target; latency SLOs we can commit to in the ring-based policy (p95 targets as above).

Approx cost ballpark (monthly, before discounts)
- Baseline (4x A100 reserved): ~$XXk/mo (we'll include exact numbers in the proposal PDF).
- Burst usage billed at reduced committed rate; we’ll include model/quantization options to reduce token cost.

Attachments sent: PulseMed_Dedicated_Capacity-Proposal.pdf (detailed config & pricing), PulseMed_MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan).

Next steps
1) I’ll share the proposal and MAP (attached) — please review with security and procurement.
2) Technical deep-dive: schedule ~60m with your infra/security + our Solutions Engineering (Dev) — suggested slots: Tue 4/13 or Wed 4/14.
3) If security requires SOC2 / pen-test artifacts, we’ll share the evidence bundle and a short security onboarding checklist before the deep-dive.

Action items for PulseMed: confirm preferred deep-dive slot and provide a procurement contact for DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to iterate on sizing once we get telemetry and concurrency numbers from your side.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifying Qs from our side after reviewing the attachments:

- Quantization / model footprint: for our clinical summarization model, how much of an efficiency lift do you expect from INT8 quantization versus FP16 in your runtime? Any tradeoffs we should be aware of for hallucination risk?
- Cost: can you include an expected committed monthly spend (number we can feed to procurement) and a short table of incremental burst pricing?
- SLA: our security team wants specifics on latency SLOs + credits model for missed SLAs (they’ll want something they can bring to legal).

Also, we’d like to bring our security lead (cc’d) into the deep-dive — is Tuesday 4/13 10:00am PT still available? If so, please send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Sara Holt
VP Product, PulseMed

Sara — great questions. Short answers below, and I’ve updated the proposal with a cost appendix (see attachment).

- Quantization: In our experience for summarization tasks, INT8 gives ~1.8-2.5x speedup and ~30-50% GPU memory reduction versus FP16 depending on model family. We surface model-quality regression tests as part of onboarding; if you need strict determinism we can run a small eval set during the trial to validate no material hallucination increase.

- Cost / committed spend: baseline reserved (4 A100) estimated at ~$28k/month in the proposal appendix. Burst pricing table is on page 6 — incremental burst is billed at a lower per-GPU/hour for committed customers. I’ll paste the key numbers into the MAP before sending to procurement.

- SLA specifics: we propose 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool and p95 latency SLO of <300ms for 512-token requests (detailed credit policy in the SLA section of the proposal). If your legal/security team wants, we can surface our standard SLA and a fallback amendment for enterprise terms.

Deep-dive: Tue 4/13 at 10:00am PT works for us. I’ll send a calendar invite with a Teams link and include a short agenda:
  1) Infra & network (VPC/KMS) checklist — 15m (Dev)
  2) Capacity profile & scaling plan — 20m (Ben / SE)
  3) SLA, compliance, and onboarding timeline — 15m (Marissa)

I’ve added links to the HubSpot deal and the Drive folder here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4581 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEFGhIjKlMNop

Next steps: I’ll send the invite and upload a trimmed evidence bundle for security ahead of the call.

Best,
Ben
